## The claim you are working on {#the-claim-you-are-working-on}

Five independent analysts reanalysed a claim made by the original author (OA) as part of the robustness study. The claim, as presented to all analysts, was:

> "…poor economic performances … decrease positive dimensions of EU framing" (Teney 2016, p. 619)

The published coefficient – the specific number that the Task 2 constraints pointed to – is:

> **Unemployment → cosmopolitan EU framing: b = −0.0034, t = −4.03, p < .001** (Table 3, Model 1)

This comes from a three-level random-intercept model using pooled Eurobarometer data (16 waves, 2004–2013, 27 EU countries). Your first job is to reproduce one of the results recorded in the robustness study for this claim, choosing among the three that rest on aggregate data (Task 3). Your second job is to deviate from the reproduced specification – deliberately, with a written justification – and see what that does to the estimate.

---

## Which claim, and why {#which-claim}

The claim on the card is one of several that the paper makes. The SCORE programme selected claims from published abstracts, and the sentence it took from this paper is the first half of a two-part hypothesis. In the paper itself, that hypothesis reads: "Poor national economic performances significantly increase the negative and decrease the positive EU-framing dimensions. The effect is stronger on the materialist dimensions of EU framing" (p. 621). The second sentence, which compares two of the four framing scales with the other two, was not part of the claim given to the analysts, and neither was the second hypothesis of the paper, about the gap between high- and low-educated citizens, which the [module on multilevel models](../../companion/multilevel.qmd#sec-claim2) takes up. The robustness study then narrowed the card further in its constrained phase, fixing the cosmopolitan scale as the outcome and the unemployment rate as the predictor, which is why the coefficient above is the one with which the five results were to be compared.

Choosing which sentence to replicate is the first specification decision of any replication, made before the estimand, the graph or the menu, usually by the people who wrote the card; the second sentence of the hypothesis needs a grouping of the scales that the data only half support, as the [measurement module](../../companion/measurement.qmd#sec-theory) shows. The course keeps to the card, so that its results can be set beside those of the five analysts.
